## Open interpretation questions for the user (no verdict rule was changed)

1. Placebo between 0.90 and 0.95: V2 sec 1 makes placebo >= 0.95 the PASS bar and >= 0.90 the CANDIDATE bar. This scorer counts a placebo in [0.90, 0.95) as the one allowed secondary failure of a CANDIDATE (strict reading); a looser reading would let such cells stay CANDIDATE with a second failure.
2. Execution-cell placebo: the placebo used for execution cells (permuted per-row delta) is conservative and uninformative for tiny paired effects (T4 says so), while V2 sec 3 judges an execution change by the paired test only. Under the letter the placebo still gates (>= 0.90); whether it should for execution cells is the open question. Affects T4.2_Y4 (placebo 0.21; also DEAD on year share > 60% and maxDD).
3. Sizing criterion branch B (mean up with maxDD not worse): read as mean up WITH CI excluding 0 (otherwise Set B would be a PASS with its CI including 0).
5. Execution cells (ruling 2026-10-25): placebo condition = paired effect >= paired MDE at 80% power (counts as placebo >= 0.95); 0.75x MDE <= effect < MDE with the paired CI excluding 0 = the one allowed secondary failure; else fail. T4 re-verdict: only T4.2_Y4 becomes CANDIDATE (year share > 60% is its one failure); T4.4_W5 stays DEAD (neighbours disagree, 2x-cost sign negative, year share > 60%); T4.2_Lm2 and T4.2_L0 stay DEAD (effect 0.54x / 0.57x MDE, CI includes 0). Flagged for the user: this is my operationalisation of the ruling.
4. Placebo of record for sleeves = min(5,000-draw WF rank, 5,000-draw pre-2024 fresh-seed rank) (NM-E convention); the original 500-draw WF rank alone would keep RSI2T/RSI2C/RSI2CC/RTY_RSI2 at PASS.
